examples.note: Provenance: the structured form total outranks the proposal text; the baseline (proposal text only) cannot see it.

Unknown chronology: no dates, revisions or supersession statement. Two figures in the same basis and scope stay unresolved; neither silently wins. Both are at or above 10, so size is established while the quantity is under review.
Explicit supersession: revision B states it supersedes revision A. Revision A is preserved as history, not deleted.
Different phases are different scopes, not a conflict. They are not added together unless non-overlap is evidenced (E38d).
A combined total exists only because explicit non-overlap evidence relates the two phases.
Approved 49 with a later proposed revision of 52. At a threshold of 50 only the proposed basis matches, and the result says so.
Revised approval: permission 2 states it supersedes permission 1; the 49 is preserved as historical evidence.

examples.proposal: OUTLINE PERMISSION FOR UP TO 50 DWELLINGS
examples.note: A qualified approved maximum keeps its qualifier everywhere, is a possible (never confirmed) match, and routes to assessment.
9 versus 12 crosses the 10+ threshold: a possible match, listed separately from confirmed matches, routed to assessment.
A form or proposal alone cannot establish an approved count: the claimed approval is recorded as unsupported and the supported proposed quantity is shown.
Alternative permissions are preserved side by side; the larger or the later does not replace the other.
The later document does not supersede the earlier one: without an explicit relationship the conflict stays unresolved.
Dwelling count, planning status and construction progress are three separate facts; none changes another.
Size eligibility is only the size gate: a refused application still has a supported proposed quantity of 49; the status gate is separate and not decided here.
9 flats plus 1 shop is 9 residential dwellings, not 10 units.
The two shops are recorded separately and do not contribute to the 10.
